line: Crowley gives Tiphareth the number 6, the Sun and the Son; Jung places Tifereth in the middle and names it the sun, but does not number it six.

sections.title: Crowley's Sixes
sections.line: The Sixes are attributed to Tiphareth, and for Crowley the number Six is the centre of the system.

quotes.quote: These cards are attributed to Tiphareth.
The Number Six, Tiphareth, as before,
Here is the number Six, the centre of the system:

sections.title: Sun and Son
sections.line: Tiphareth is the Sun in the planetary system and the Son in the system of Tetragrammaton.

quotes.quote: In the planetary system it represents the Sun;
in the system of Tetragrammaton it represents the Son.

sections.title: The direct line and the airy Sephira
sections.line: Crowley says Tiphareth alone of the sephiroth below the Abyss communicates directly with Kether, and that the Ruach is centred in it.

quotes.quote: The Ruach is centred in the airy Sephira, Tiphareth, who is the Son,

sections.title: Jung's order and the sun
sections.line: Jung's arrangement, Kether, Tifereth, Yesod, Malchuth, puts Tifereth second, not sixth, and he does not number it. The tie to the Self rests on Jung naming Tifereth the middle position and the sun; the site reads that as the centre the Self occupies, which Jung does not say.

quotes.quote: in the usual arrangement of the Sefiroth he occupies the second place
The figure of Tifereth belongs to the Sefiroth system, which is conceived to be a tree. Tifereth occupies the middle position
Yesod is as a part to the whole, and the whole is Tifereth, who is named the sun
